chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
Everything that flies—there is no harm in its droppings and its urine.

key_terms.بَوْلِهِ: its urine; the urine of the flying creature
key_terms.خُرْئِهِ: its droppings; the excrement of the flying creature
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicates permissibility and absence of objection
key_terms.يَطِيرُ: flies; refers to creatures characterized by flight

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the droppings and urine of birds in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity. It states that the droppings and urine of creatures that fly are not objectionable, indicating they are treated as ritually pure in this context.
